claims.body: The Senators are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Bruins are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Senators’ chance quality wins out.

claims.head: There’s no curse: Swayman vs. The Senators
claims.body: Swayman has been shaky against the Senators since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
claims.nums: 5 starts against Ottawa: .863 save percentage · .906 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Swayman’s record against the Senators.
claims.call: If Swayman starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .906 than to his .863 against the Senators.

claims.head: The Bruins can’t afford to take penalties
claims.call: The Senators’ power play creates at least their usual 7.9 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Senators’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Bruins’ kill is near the bottom. Every trip to the box hurts the Bruins more than most. The Bruins take a lot of penalties and the Senators draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

claims.head: Who drives the play: the Senators
claims.body: The Senators have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Bruins around the middle. Expect the Senators to spend more of the night in the Bruins’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.
claims.call: The Senators get the bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances.
claims.nums: Share of 5-on-5 expected goals: Ottawa 55.7%, Boston 49.8%
claims.gist: The Senators usually control more of the chances than the Bruins do.

stakes: The Senators go in tied for fourth in the Atlantic with 2 points, 2 points behind the Bruins, tied for first. A regulation win for the Senators would pull them level with the Bruins. The Senators have two games in hand.

BOS.head: The Bruins face a real test
BOS.body: Even though Boston has home-ice advantage, Ottawa has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Bruins’ best way through is keeping shots to a minimum.

OTT.head: Advantage, the Senators
OTT.body: Even though Boston has home-ice advantage, Ottawa has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Bruins’ way back in is keeping shots to a minimum.

story.head: Unstoppable force vs. Immovable object
paras: The Senators come in at 1-0-0, the Bruins at 2-1-0.

items.text: Claude Giroux has scored in five straight games against Boston.
The Senators have been without Jake Sanderson and Ridly Greig all season. Counting how much each missing player usually brings, only the Ducks and the Islanders are missing more right now.
The Bruins have been without Charlie McAvoy all season.
Tim Stützle is one point from passing Wade Redden for sixth on the Senators’ all-time scoring list.
